name: copulas
prompt: This repository is a knowledge kernel; you are auditing part of its own mathematics. `COPULAS` in pw/credal.py gives, for each class of copulas, the range of the probability that several pieces of evidence are all observed. Do not change pw/credal.py. Establish the required claim. The function to model takes a non-empty list p of probabilities and returns the triple (lower end under 'frechet', value under 'independent', upper end under 'pqd'), i.e. COPULAS['frechet'](p, p)[0], COPULAS['independent'](p, p)[0], COPULAS['pqd'](p, p)[1] with p = numpy.array(<list of fractions.Fraction>, dtype=object) so that the arithmetic is exact. State the binding so: the call takes one argument with domain "units" (a list of Fractions). Lean here has Mathlib.

requires.subject: pw/credal.py::COPULAS
requires.gloss: for probabilities, Frechet lower bound <= product <= minimum: the copula classes nest

name: exchange
prompt: This repository is a knowledge kernel; you are auditing part of its own mathematics. `exchangeable_agreement(k, mean, min_concentration)` in pw/credal.py returns (lo, hi), bounds on the probability that k random checks all agree although the hypothesis is false. Do not change pw/credal.py. Establish the required claim. State the binding with domains ["nat", "unit", "pos"]; the rational arguments arrive as fractions.Fraction, so the arithmetic is exact. Lean here has Mathlib.

requires.subject: pw/credal.py::exchangeable_agreement
requires.gloss: the agreement bounds are ordered probabilities, the upper one is worst at the least concentration, and the uniform prior gives 1/(k+1)

name: metric
prompt: This repository is a knowledge kernel; you are checking a statement from its documentation. docs/symbols.md section 6 says that the distance d(A, B) = probability that A and B disagree satisfies the triangle inequality. Establish the required claim: state it as a closed Lean proposition with `ground` (finite set of worlds, non-negative rational weights) and prove it. There is no code to model. Lean here has Mathlib.
requires: For every probability distribution on a finite set of worlds and all events A, B, C, the probability that A and C disagree is at most the probability that A and B disagree plus the probability that B and C disagree
